bio: Just a few metres from Parque Eduardo VII, you’ll find MITSU, an intimate restaurant with only 10 seats at the counter facing the chef and four seats at the small tables around the room. The experience is led by chef Shinya Koike and his right-hand man, Kshetri Raju, and together they offer a one-of-a-kind omakase experience, built around exceptional produce sourced mainly from the waters of Setúbal, Nazareth and the Azores. From the menu, featuring Maki, Futomaki, Sashimi, Nigiri and Onigiri, we’d single out the Ostra com molho ponzu e nabo, oyster with ponzu sauce and turnip, with fresh citrus notes that pair perfectly with the oyster’s briny, iodine-rich flavour. Did you know? The name MITSU means something sweet or flavoursome in Japanese, making it an ideal spot for anyone in search of surprising flavours!
